name: TMUX4051PWRQ1
title: Automotive 24 V, 8:1 one-channel and 4:1 two-channel multiplexers with 1.8 V logic
summary: TMUX4051-Q1 (8:1, one channel) and TMUX4052-Q1 (4:1, two channels) are AEC-Q100 CMOS analog multiplexers for single supplies of 5 V to 24 V or split rails up to ±12 V. Signals pass in either direction anywhere between the rails, with about 60 Ω to 75 Ω on-resistance and 3 pF source capacitance. Address and active-low enable inputs accept 1.8 V logic; switching is break-before-make. Pinouts follow the 4051 and 4052.
key_figures: 5 V to 24 V single, up to ±12 V dual
75 Ω typ at VDD = 5 V; 60 Ω typ at 24 V
VIH 1.35 V min, VIL 0.8 V max

circuits.title: Eight signals multiplexed into a microcontroller's integrated ADC
circuits.description: System voltages reach the source pins: two LDO outputs on S0 and S1 and two LM20 temperature sensor outputs on S6 and S7, with S2 to S5 free for further inputs such as a third LDO or another LM20. The common drain D feeds one ADC input of the microcontroller, which sets A0, A1 and A2 from 1.8 V logic outputs to choose the channel; EN is grounded so the mux is always enabled. VDD and VSS each carry a decoupling capacitor to ground. In the worked example VDD is 12 V and any signal from 0 V to 12 V passes. The TMUX4052-Q1 serves the same purpose for differential pairs, or as a pair of independent 4:1 muxes.

parts.value: MCU with integrated 12-bit ADC and 1.8 V logic I/O

notes: Misprint: inputs S1 to S8 should read S0 to S7.
Decoupling from 0.1 µF to 10 µF is recommended on each supply pin; 0.1 µF is the value given for layout.

circuits.description: S0 and S7 both sit at VDD and S1 to S6 are grounded. Toggling all three address lines at once moves D from S0 to S7 and back; the output dips while neither switch is closed, and tBBM is the shorter of the two dips measured at the 90% level.

operation.text: The TMUX4051-Q1 routes one of eight sources S0 to S7 to a single drain D. The TMUX4052-Q1 is a pair of 4:1 muxes, A and B, that switch together (S0A to S3A onto DA, S0B to S3B onto DB), suited to differential signals.

Runs from one 5 V to 24 V rail, from split rails as far as ±12 V, or from uneven rails such as VDD = 12 V with VSS = –5 V. VDD – VSS must lie from 5 V to 24 V. AEC-Q100 qualified, temperature grade 1 (–40°C to 125°C ambient); operating range –55°C to 125°C.

Every switch conducts equally in both directions, so the part works as a mux or a demux. Signals may swing anywhere from VSS to VDD. Switching is break-before-make. Signal pins are clamped to the rails by diodes.

A0 to A2 and EN have 1.8 V compatible thresholds (VIH 1.35 V minimum, VIL 0.8 V maximum) at every valid supply, so they accept TTL and CMOS levels and 1.8 V processors drive them without a level shifter. EN is active low: high opens every switch whatever the address; low closes the one switch (or pair) the address picks.
Tie unused logic inputs to GND or VDD; a floating CMOS input raises supply current. Connect unused Sx and Dx pins to GND. With the enable function not needed, ground EN.
Only supply decoupling is needed. All signals through the mux must stay within the recommended signal range and continuous current.

Fit a 0.1 µF to 10 µF ceramic (MLCC, low ESR and ESL) from VDD to ground and from VSS to ground, as near the pins as possible with low-impedance connections. In sensitive or noisy systems, connect the capacitors without vias; several vias in parallel lower inductance into a ground plane.

Decouple VDD and VSS with 0.1 µF placed at the pins, rated for the supply voltage. Keep input traces short. Use an unbroken ground plane. Route fast signals with few vias and corners; give any via extra clearance to cut its capacitance; avoid through-hole test points at high frequency. Keep analog traces away from digital ones and cross them only at right angles. Power traces are wide for low inductance.
The WQFN exposed pad has no internal connection; float it or tie it to GND. It is soldered to the board for thermal and mechanical performance.
TMUX4051 and TMUX4052 are the catalog grades of these parts; TMUX405x is pin compatible with the industry-standard 4051 and 4052.
